entries.title: strlen
entries.summary: Length of a string, without the terminator.
entries.description: Counts the characters before the `'\0'`. It walks the whole string each time: do not call it in a loop condition on a long string.
mistakes: Allocating `strlen(s)` bytes for a copy (you need +1).

entries.title: strcpy
entries.summary: Copy a string, including its terminator.
entries.description: `dst` must be big enough for `strlen(src) + 1` bytes: nothing checks it. Returns `dst`.

entries.title: strncpy
entries.summary: Copy at most n characters of a string.
entries.description: If `src` has `n` or more characters, `dst` is NOT terminated; if it has fewer, the rest of `n` bytes is padded with zeros. Terminate it yourself: `dst[n - 1] = '\0'`.
entries.example:
strncpy(dst, src, sizeof dst - 1);
dst[sizeof dst - 1] = '\0';
mistakes: Assuming the result is always a valid string.

entries.title: strcat
entries.description: Copies `src` after the end of `dst`. The destination must have room for both strings plus the terminator.

entries.title: strncat
entries.summary: Append at most n characters of a string.
entries.description: Appends at most `n` characters and always adds the terminator, so `dst` needs `strlen(dst) + n + 1` bytes.

entries.title: strcmp
entries.description: Returns 0 if they are equal, a negative number if `a` comes before `b` and a positive one otherwise (character codes decide). Use it for equality and ordering, never `==`.
entries.example:
if (strcmp(argv[1], "-h") == 0) { /* equal */ }
qsort(names, n, sizeof *names, cmp);   /* cmp uses strcmp */
mistakes: Reading `strcmp` as true when equal: it returns 0 then.

entries.title: strncmp
entries.summary: Compare at most the first n characters.
entries.syntax: int strncmp(const char *a, const char *b, size_t n);
entries.description: Like `strcmp` but stops after `n` characters: handy for prefixes.

entries.title: strchr
entries.summary: Find the first occurrence of a character.
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the first `c` in `s`, or NULL. `strchr(s, '\0')` points to the terminator.
mistakes: Using the result without checking for NULL.

entries.title: strrchr
entries.summary: Find the last occurrence of a character.
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the last `c` in `s`, or NULL. Typical use: the extension or the file name in a path.

entries.title: strstr
entries.summary: Find the first occurrence of a substring.
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the start of the first match, or NULL.

entries.title: strdup
entries.summary: Make a heap copy of a string.
entries.description: Allocates `strlen(s) + 1` bytes with `malloc` and copies `s`. You must `free` the copy. Returns NULL if out of memory.

entries.title: strtok
entries.summary: Split a string into tokens (modifies it).
entries.description: The first call gets the string, later calls get NULL. It writes `'\0'` into the string, so it needs a modifiable copy (never a literal), and it keeps hidden state, so it is not usable in two loops at once. Skips empty fields.

entries.title: strtok_r
entries.summary: strtok with the state kept in a variable you provide.
entries.description: Same splitting as `strtok`, but safe to nest and to use from several threads. Pass the same `saveptr` on every call of one loop.

entries.title: strcspn
entries.summary: Length of the initial part of a string that has none of the given characters.
entries.description: Returns the index of the first character of `s` that is in `reject` (or `strlen(s)` if none). Common idiom to strip a newline: `s[strcspn(s, "\n")] = '\0';`.

entries.title: strspn
entries.summary: Length of the initial part of a string made only of the given characters.
entries.description: Returns how many characters at the start of `s` are all in `accept`.
